metadata.name: sythstaking
metadata.description: Synthetic Staking V2 Protocol by Luminosity Labs

instructions.name: cancel_unstake
docs: Leave the redemption queue before being settled: re-mint the claimer's
receipt tokens and drop the payout from `pending_payouts`, restoring the
caller to their exact pre-`unstake` position. This is the escape hatch for
a queue that has stalled (e.g. the strategy has not returned funds) so a
burned-receipt holder is never stranded.
`user_receipt_ata` is created if it does not already exist
(`init_if_needed`, payer = the signer). After `unstake` the receipt balance
is zero but the ATA normally remains open; if the claimer closed that empty
account, cancellation still succeeds - no separate ATA-creation transaction
is needed.
The record is only flagged here (not closed) so it can still serve as the
FIFO marker; `settle` advances the head over it and refunds the rent. The
max-supply cap is intentionally not re-checked - this restores receipts
that already existed, it does not issue new ones.

accounts.name: user_receipt_ata
docs: Claimer's receipt ATA — created if needed so a user who closed their
empty ATA after `unstake` can still cancel without a separate tx.

instructions.name: claim
docs: Pull a settled claim's payout from the pool to the claimer and close the
claim record, refunding the prepaid rent to the claimer. Permissionless -
anyone can trigger it, but funds always go to the claimer's account. A
claim must be `settle`d first; an unusable claimer account only stalls this
one claim, never the queue.

instructions.name: create_pool
docs: Create a new staking pool together with its self-authority receipt mint
and the pool's stake token ATA. Admin-only.
The pool's stake token is the passed `stake_mint` (use the WSOL mint for a
SOL pool), and the receipt mint inherits its decimals so rates stay 1:1 in
display units. The receipt mint is a PDA seeded by the pool key; its mint
and freeze authority are the mint itself, so only this program can change
supply. The pool's stake ATA is created here (admin pays rent) so the first
staker is not surprised by an extra SOL cost.

accounts.name: stake_mint
docs: Mint that stakers deposit; the receipt mint inherits its decimals.

accounts.name: pool_stake_ata
docs: Pool's stake token ATA — created here so the admin pays rent instead of
the first staker.

instructions.name: execute_withdraw
docs: Manager executes the pending withdrawal once its timelock has elapsed and
the strategy is active. The reserve is re-checked against live balances.

instructions.name: initialize
docs: Create the global config. Callable once, only by the program's upgrade
authority; the `init` constraint prevents re-initialization.
`withdraw_delay` (seconds) is the timelock applied to strategy changes and
withdrawals.

instructions.name: propose_strategy
docs: Admin proposes the pool's withdrawal destination (a strategy/custody
wallet). It becomes usable only after `withdraw_delay`, and withdrawals
can only ever go to this allowlisted address.

instructions.name: request_withdraw
docs: Manager requests a withdrawal of `amount` to the pool's strategy. The
amount must leave the required reserve intact, and the request can only be
executed after `withdraw_delay` so LPs can react.

instructions.name: set_rates
docs: Update stake / unstake rates. The oracle is the pool's price feed and is
the only authority over rates; the manager has no say here.

instructions.name: settle
docs: Settle the FIFO-head claim: confirm the pool holds enough to back it, move
its payout from the `pending` bucket to the `settled` bucket, and advance
the head. Bookkeeping only - no tokens move, so this step can never be
blocked by a frozen/closed claimer destination. Permissionless; a keeper
drains the queue in order as liquidity allows.
If the head claim was cancelled (the claimer left the queue via
`cancel_unstake`), it carries no obligation: this just advances the head
past it and closes the record, refunding the prepaid rent to the claimer.
That requires no liquidity, so a cancelled claim can never stall the queue.

accounts.name: claimer
docs: claim was cancelled.

instructions.name: stake
docs: Stake the pool's `stake_token` (WSOL, USDC, ...) and mint receipt tokens
(LMNSSol, LUSDC, ...) to the staker. `min_receipt_out` guards against the
stake rate moving between submission and execution.

instructions.name: stake_with_referral
docs: `stake`, plus an optional referral id that is echoed in the `Staked`
event. A separate instruction on purpose: `stake`'s wire format stays
byte-identical, so clients that never pass a referral id keep working
against the upgraded program without a code change.

instructions.name: unstake
docs: Burn the staker's receipt tokens and open a `ClaimRecord` for the payout.
The staker pays the claim record's rent up front and gets it back when the
claim is claimed. The payout rate is locked in here, so `min_payout_out`
guards against the unstake rate moving between submission and execution.

instructions.name: unstake_with_referral
docs: `unstake`, plus an optional referral id echoed in the `Unstaked` event.
Separate instruction so `unstake`'s wire format never changes. The id is
not stored: it is an attestation of the period's end, paired off-chain
with the matching `Staked`. A later `cancel_unstake` voids the period.

instructions.name: update_global
docs: Update global config. Callable only by the current admin. Either field may
be left as `None` to keep its current value.

instructions.name: update_limit
docs: Manager updates `receipt_max_supply`.

instructions.name: update_min_deposit
docs: Manager updates the minimum deposit amount for a pool. `0` disables the
floor. No upper bound is enforced — the manager is trusted and the value
is observable on-chain via the emitted event.

types.name: ClaimRecord
docs: A pending unstake payout, opened on `unstake`, marked on `settle`, and closed
on `claim` (PDA: `["claim", pool_id, nonce]`).

fields.name: claimer
docs: Wallet entitled to the payout and the rent refund.

fields.name: receipt_amount
docs: Receipt tokens burned; re-minted to the claimer if the claim is cancelled.

fields.name: payout
docs: Stake-token payout, computed and frozen at unstake time so later rate
changes never apply to an already-open claim.

fields.name: settled
docs: True once the claim has reached the FIFO head and been reserved in the
`settled_payouts` bucket; the claimer can then pull it via `claim`.

fields.name: cancelled
docs: True if the claimer withdrew from the queue via `cancel_unstake` (receipts
re-minted, obligation removed). The record lingers only as a FIFO marker
until `settle` advances the head past it, then it is closed.

types.name: Global
docs: Singleton program config (PDA: `["global"]`).

fields.name: admin
docs: Authority allowed to create pools, rotate this admin, and set strategies.

fields.name: count
docs: Number of pools created so far; doubles as the next pool's id.

fields.name: withdraw_delay
docs: Delay (seconds) enforced on strategy changes and withdrawals so LPs can
see capital movements coming and exit first.

types.name: Pool
docs: A staking pool (PDA: `["pool", id]`).

fields.name: manager
docs: Runs the timelocked withdrawal flow and updates the deposit cap.

fields.name: oracle
docs: Price-feed key; the sole authority over stake / unstake rates.

fields.name: stake_token
docs: Mint deposited by stakers (the WSOL mint for a SOL pool).

fields.name: receipt_token
docs: Self-authority yield mint handed out to stakers.

fields.name: stake_rate
docs: Stake-token per receipt-token rate, scaled by `RATE_DENOM`.

fields.name: unstake_rate
docs: Receipt-token to stake-token payout rate, scaled by `RATE_DENOM`.

fields.name: receipt_max_supply
docs: Cap on the receipt token's total supply; this bounds total deposits.

fields.name: nonce
docs: Next nonce to assign; bumped on every `unstake`.

fields.name: settle_head
docs: Nonce of the next claim that must be settled. Enforces FIFO redemption:
claims are settled strictly in the order they were opened.

fields.name: pending_payouts
docs: Stake-token owed across open claims that have not yet been settled (still
waiting in the FIFO queue for liquidity).

fields.name: settled_payouts
docs: Stake-token owed across settled claims that the claimer has not yet pulled.
Reserved in the pool and never withdrawable to a strategy.

fields.name: reserve_bps
docs: Fraction (bps) of still-staked liabilities that must stay in the pool, on
top of `settled_payouts`, and can never be swept to a strategy.

fields.name: strategy
docs: Allowlisted withdrawal destination (strategy/custody wallet). Withdrawals
can only ever go here; `None` until a strategy is proposed.

fields.name: strategy_activates_at
docs: Unix time at which the current `strategy` becomes usable.

fields.name: pending_withdraw_amount
docs: Amount of the pending withdrawal request (0 if none).

fields.name: withdraw_unlocks_at
docs: Unix time at which the pending withdrawal may be executed.

fields.name: receipt_bump
docs: Bump for the self-authority receipt mint PDA (seeded by the pool key).

fields.name: min_deposit_amount
docs: Minimum stake-token amount per deposit. Deposits below this are rejected.
Kept last on purpose. Pools created before this field existed are 8 bytes
shorter than `INIT_SPACE`, and borsh reads a trailing field out of the
account's zero padding — so an old pool decodes with a `0` floor (i.e.
disabled) and every preceding field, including `bump`, stays at its
original offset. Inserting it mid-struct instead shifts `bump` and
silently bricks those pools. **Append new fields here; never insert.**
The padding this relies on comes from `strategy: Option<Pubkey>` being
`None` on those legacy accounts: `InitSpace` reserves 33 bytes, borsh
writes 1. Once a legacy pool sets a strategy it needs the full 269 bytes
it was never allocated, so such a pool must be re-created (or realloc'd)
before `propose_strategy`. Pools created from now on are sized correctly.

types.name: Staked
docs: Emitted on every stake, referred or not.
**Append-only fields.** Existing decoders read the prefix they know and
ignore any tail, so new fields may only be added at the end. Inserting one
shifts every later field for every already-deployed decoder - the same trap
`Pool` documents on the account side.

fields.name: ts
docs: Unix time the stake was credited. With `Unstaked.ts` this bounds the
period a referral can claim yield for; the block time alone is not
reliable, since it can be absent on some slots.

fields.name: stake_rate
docs: Pool `stake_rate` at credit time (`RATE_DENOM` scale), so the period's
yield is derivable from attested values alone.

fields.name: referral_id
docs: Referrer id when the stake was referred via `stake_with_referral`;
`None` for every ordinary `stake`, so unrelated history is unchanged.

types.name: Unstaked
docs: Emitted on every unstake, referred or not. Field order is **append-only**;
see the note on `Staked`.

fields.name: ts
docs: Unix time the redemption was opened (the period's end).

fields.name: unstake_rate
docs: Pool `unstake_rate` at redemption time (`RATE_DENOM` scale).

fields.name: referral_id
docs: Referrer id carried through from `stake_with_referral`, if any. A
subsequent `cancel_unstake` voids the period.
